# ASA Industry News Pulse — 2026-11-02

**Reporting interval:** 2026-10-30T06:30:00-07:00 to 2026-11-02T06:30:00-08:00
**Candidates classified:** 34
**Material signals:** 2

## Top summary

Two material signals cleared the interval: Jack Henry expanded distribution of its treasury-management platform to all ICBA members, strengthening a channel partner’s commercial-finance reach adjacent to ASA’s One View and Forecast products[1]; separately, Senator Elizabeth Warren asked DOJ to investigate Bank of America’s AML failures, reinforcing elevated expectations for AML controls, monitoring, sanctions compliance, and data governance[2].

## Material signals

### Jack Henry expands treasury-management distribution through ICBA

Jack Henry’s treasury-management solution is now available to all ICBA members through the organization’s Preferred Service Provider program[1]. The broader distribution strengthens Jack Henry’s commercial-finance capabilities and increases competitive adjacency to ASA’s transaction-visibility and cash-flow-forecasting products[1].

### Warren seeks DOJ investigation into Bank of America AML failures

Senator Elizabeth Warren asked DOJ to conduct a criminal investigation into Bank of America’s AML and sanctions-law violations following recent regulatory penalties[2]. She requested clarification by November 12 on whether DOJ has investigated or plans to investigate the conduct; DOJ did not confirm or deny an ongoing investigation[2]. The development reinforces heightened AML, monitoring, sanctions-control, and data-governance expectations relevant to ASA’s financial-institution roadmap[2].

## Candidate disposition

Both supplied material candidates are retained as distinct, evidence-backed events. No candidate was excluded as a duplicate. Monitor, noise, and needs-validation items remain outside the material section; the 17 needs-validation items remain blocked pending additional validation.
